classification.difficultyReason: Substitute the explicit relationship r=2h into cone volume, recognise the supplied sphere comparison and differentiate the resulting cubic before substitution.

content.prompt: Sand is poured at a rate of $0.5\text{ m}^3/\text{s}$ onto the top of a pile in the shape of a cone, as shown in the diagram. Let the base have radius $r$, and let the height of the cone be $h$. The pile always remains in the same shape, with $r=2h$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the cone’s volume in terms of $h$, and show that it is the same as the volume of a sphere whose radius is equal to the cone’s height.

spec.description: Upright cone with elliptical base, perpendicular height and a radius to the right rim. Source yellow base fill is omitted under the house unshaded geometry policy; the complete base outline remains.
spec.mathematics: Apex vertically above the base centre; height h is perpendicular to radius r; r=2h is supplied in the stem.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent student givens.

answer.short: $V=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}h^3$, equal to the volume of a sphere of radius $h$.
answer.worked:
Since $r=2h$,
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\&=\frac13\pi(2h)^2h\\&=\frac13\pi(4h^2)h\\&=\frac{4\pi}{3}h^3.\end{aligned}$$
A sphere of radius $h$ has volume $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}h^3$, so the volumes are equal.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the height is increasing when the radius of the base is 4 metres.
